name: Pale Violet Red
lede: Pale Violet Red is a mid pink-red named in the X11 and CSS color lists, where it is written as one word, `palevioletred`.

sections.title: A list name
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary files PaleVioletRed as one of the colors in the X11 Color Set and gives its hex code as #DB7093 [1]. The same book lists it among the reds, with the asterisk it uses for X11 names [2]. It is a computer-era name, written in the CSS style without spaces or hyphens [1].

The books say nothing more about it: no dye, flower or maker is tied to this name [1][2]. The words in it are ordinary color words, though. Our library puts the swatch closest to a deep purplish pink in the ISCC-NBS naming of 1955 [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch is #DB7093, a medium-light pink-red with a hint of blue [3]. In our archive of 23,781 paintings, only one has this color covering at least 5% of the canvas: Kirchner's *Two Girls under an Umbrella*, painted in 1910 [4]. That makes it rarer than 86% of named colors, as photographed [4]. A single painting is a thin base, so read it as a note about the archive, not about painters [4].

questions.q: Which color list is Pale Violet Red named in?
True or false: the books tie Pale Violet Red to a particular dye.

openers: Pale Violet Red is a computer-list name, not a dye: the books say only that it belongs to the X11 set.

issues: Claims verified against fact card and book text; no changes.
